title: Gregory's letter to Mellitus says to keep the temples and destroy the idols inside them
summary: In 601 Gregory tells Mellitus to keep English temples and remove the idols inside them.
body: Gregory's letter tells Mellitus not to destroy the temples of the gods of the English, but rather the idols within those temples, and then to place altars and relics there. The letter is a papal instruction about conversion. It is not Bede's later narrative of the same mission, though Bede reports the mission. The wording on the page includes: "Augustine that he should be no means destroy the temples of the gods but rather the idols within those temples. Let him, after he has purified them with holy water, place altars and relics of the saints in them. For, if those temples are well built, they should be converted from the worship of demons to the service of the true God. Thus, seeing that their places of". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
